title: Keep review changes and external review collections complete after reload
description:
## Context
Review manager failures could leave mutation state inconsistent, rejected operations were not uniformly retained for retry, seven public templates reduced external review pages to one link, and the completed external-review collection lacked an owner-managed visible section title. The final parity audit hardens mutation failure handling, preserves complete ordered collections, and gives owners one safe heading that is projected to every public template without invented template copy.

## User story
As a profile owner, I need review edits, every saved external review page, and my chosen section title to persist in their intended order so the public bio matches the dashboard after reload.

## Acceptance criteria
- Review and external-page create, update, visibility, reorder, and delete reload the preview exactly once after authoritative success and zero times after returned or thrown failure.
- Failed operations retain a usable retry state and do not leave controls permanently busy.
- Public templates render every valid enabled external review page in deterministic rank-and-ID order.
- The dashboard accepts a normalized optional external-review section title and retains its draft on failure.
- All nine templates display the owner-authored title when configured, use no hardcoded public fallback heading, and keep blank-title links accessible.
- The private dentistry value synchronizes through the read-only public_profiles projection; the owner/admin RPC and generated types preserve that boundary.
- Focused manager, action, query, component, database-boundary, pgTAP, and dashboard/public reload coverage pass.

## References
- Branch: codex/public-profile-feature-parity
- Fixing commits: 2f2f1925, 5fa2c24c, 0161f7f0
- Boundary/type evidence: 6d3f35af, 9440b805, 6f13b42c
- Final source/evidence head: 1a4621cb18912ce45dc5f1a013b9e1d7e2020265
- Final pull request: https://github.com/digimaxhub/dentalbio/pull/136
- Scope: final public-profile parity audit remediation

title: Keep aggregate template seed verification aligned with parity data
description:
## Context
The aggregate local-seed verifier still assumed the earlier showcase shapes after the parity overlays added complete treatment, service, location, media, and owner-authored data. Every feature-specific verifier passed, but the aggregate verifier rejected the same correct clean seed and made release evidence contradictory.

## User story
As a maintainer, I need the aggregate seed check to validate the current deterministic showcase contract so a clean local reset gives one trustworthy parity result.

## Acceptance criteria
- The aggregate verifier checks the Pro account, Admin account, and all nine showcase profiles after every parity overlay.
- Representative IDs, ownership, ordering, enabled state, and expected content remain strict rather than being weakened to counts alone.
- Location and storage checks use stable owner-scoped entities and the validated isolated Storage origin.
- The verifier works with an isolated Supabase workdir and rejects invalid or mismatched origins.
- A clean seeded reset passes the aggregate verifier and all focused verifier-status tests.

## References

title: Keep database contract tests isolated and scheduler-independent
description:
## Context
The full pgTAP suite depended on a host-specific database port, collided with shared fixture IDs and seeded ranks, used a stale link result shape, attempted an illegal Vault mutation, and expected one possible concurrency completion order. Correct application behavior could therefore fail when the suite ran on another isolated stack or the scheduler completed the second request first.

## User story
As a maintainer, I need database contract tests to be isolated, portable, and insensitive to valid scheduler order so release gates report actual database regressions.

## Acceptance criteria
- dblink concurrency tests connect through the internal Supabase database hostname and port rather than a host-machine port.
- Test users, dentistries, blogs, treatments, and links use unique owner-scoped fixtures that do not collide with deterministic seeds.
- Link concurrency consumes the current result shape and proves both requested rows plus contiguous ranks without assuming which request finishes first.
- Webhook contract tests preserve protected Vault ciphertext and still prove the intended secret boundary.
- The admin funnel expectation matches the complete authoritative history.
- A fresh isolated stack passes every pgTAP file and assertion.

## References
- Branch: codex/public-profile-feature-parity
- Fixing commits: 1141bdcc, dc5caaa7
- Independent review: .superpowers/sdd/MASTER_GOAL/reviews/full-pgtap-portability-review-1141bdcc.md
- Final source/evidence head: 1a4621cb18912ce45dc5f1a013b9e1d7e2020265
- Final pull request: https://github.com/digimaxhub/dentalbio/pull/136
- Scope: final database verification reliability

title: Keep shared-template contract tests aligned with component reuse
description:
## Context
Several static parity tests still searched parent template source for anchors and implementation text that had correctly moved into shared treatment, service, link, location, video, product, and review components. The rendered product contract was valid, but the stale tests rejected the encouraged component-reuse architecture.

## User story
As a maintainer, I need static template contracts to verify composition and shared ownership at the correct boundary so component reuse does not create false release failures.

## Acceptance criteria
- Parent-template checks prove the expected shared component is composed exactly where required.
- Anchor, location-consumer, preview-target, video, product, treatment, service, and link assertions inspect the shared owner of the behavior.
- Mutation failure, retained-draft, reload, persistence, and duplicate-guard checks remain exact.
- Focused static contracts pass without weakening runtime behavior or adding template-specific duplicates.

title: Keep loaded interaction tests reliable in the full unit suite
description:
## Context
The registration submission and shared-card interaction tests passed alone but could exceed a narrow default timing bound during the loaded full unit run. The resulting false failures obscured the status of otherwise valid interaction behavior.

## User story
As a maintainer, I need interaction tests to tolerate realistic aggregate-suite load while keeping their behavior assertions strict so the full unit gate remains trustworthy.

## Acceptance criteria
- Only the two reproduced load-sensitive interaction cases receive a bounded explicit test timeout.
- Assertions for registration submission and shared-card behavior remain unchanged.
- Focused tests pass and the final full unit suite completes without the prior timing-only failures.
- No production timeout, retry, or user-facing behavior is changed.
